dev.title: Build DSG into your emulator
dev.lead: One request tells you which mods exist for the game the user is about to boot — with download URLs, checksums and machine-readable install steps.
dev.step1: Identify the game: ROM hash (sha1, md5, crc32), title id, disc serial or store id.
dev.step2: Call /v1/lookup with it, plus your emulator id, version and the device.
dev.step3: Download the assets from the author's GitHub release and verify the sha256.
dev.step4: Run the install steps, mapping path variables such as {var} to your folders.

ep.lookup: Game + compatible mods from a hash, title id, serial or store id
ep.latest: Download URLs, sizes, sha256 and install steps
ep.mods: Filter by game, type, platform, emulator, device
ep.index: Everything at once, for offline caches (ETag)

dev.userAgent: Send a User-Agent naming your app. The API is read-only, CORS-enabled and rate limited.
dev.offline: Prefer an offline cache? Mirror /v1/index.json and revalidate with If-None-Match.

submit.title: Add your mod to DSG
submit.lead: Mods are listed through small YAML manifests reviewed as pull requests. DSG never re-hosts your files: it links to your GitHub releases.
submit.step1: Publish your mod as a GitHub release with the files attached.
submit.step2: Fork the DSG repository and add registry/mods/<your-mod>.yaml (and the game under registry/games/ if it is new).
submit.step3: Run pnpm registry:validate, then open a pull request. CI checks it automatically.
submit.step4: Once merged, new releases you publish appear on DSG automatically.
submit.imagesBody: DSG picks up the images in your README, your release notes and image files attached to the release. Name a pair like map-top.png and map-bottom.png (or list them under previews) and they are shown together on the two-screen preview.
